title: test(app): fixture_library folder resolver uses host-absolute paths
body:
## What changed

`crates/app/tests/fixture_library.rs`, test `the_library_folder_is_the_override_else_a_sibling_of_machines` only. No product code.

The test fed Unix-only paths (`/shop/fixtures`, `/Users/me`, `/home/me`). `fixture_library::user_dir_for` (`store.rs`) keeps an override only when `PathBuf::is_absolute()` is true on the host, so on a Windows host those paths were dropped and the assertions failed.

- The override path, the macOS HOME and the linux HOME are now picked per OS with `cfg!(windows)` (`C:\shop\fixtures`, `C:\Users\me`, `C:\home\me` on Windows; the old strings elsewhere), the same pattern as `machine_edit.rs` `the_user_folder_resolves_from_the_override_else_the_platform_data_folder`.
- Expected folders are built with `PathBuf::from(home).join(...)`, so separators are right on both hosts.
- The `env` helper now copies its pairs into owned strings instead of requiring `&'static` literals, so runtime-chosen per-OS strings can be passed.
- Assertions keep their meaning: an absolute override wins; a relative override (`"relative"`) falls back to HOME; the macOS and linux data folders are unchanged; `linux` with no HOME gives `None`. `library_path(&PathBuf::from("/x"))` is unchanged: it only checks the file name suffix, which holds on any host.

## Why it passes on Windows

On Windows the three host-absolute paths are absolute, so `CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES` is kept and the HOME branches resolve under `C:\Users\me` / `C:\home\me`. The relative override stays non-absolute on Windows too, so it falls back to HOME. The expected `PathBuf`s are built from the same strings with `join`, so they compare equal to what `user_dir_for` produces. This is the same construction as `machine_edit.rs`, which already passes in the Windows batch.

## How tested

- macOS: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test fixture_library -- the_library_folder_is_the_override_else_a_sibling_of_machines --exact` - 1 passed.
- macOS: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test fixture_library -- -D warnings` - clean.
- Linux quick gate against upstream main: `app fixture_library (1 fn)` ok.
- Pinning test: `fixture_library::the_library_folder_is_the_override_else_a_sibling_of_machines`.

## Not exercised

- No Windows run. This repo has no Windows machine on our side; the maintainer's Windows batch confirms the test passes there.
- The other `fixture_library` tests and the full suite were not run in this PR (the quick gate ran the changed test binary only).

title: feat(wcs): anchor the WCS on a picked circle's centre; tidy the WCS page
body:
## What changed

**Shared pick primitive** - `crates/app/src/pick/circle.rs` (next to the #692 pick graph): `circle_centre(world, &GeoSel)`, `circle_of_edge(graph, edge)`, `circle_of_run(features, run)` return a `Circle { centre, axis, radius, closed }` or a named `CircleRefusal` (`Straight`, `TooShort`, `NotCircular`, `NotAnEdge`, `Gone`). The edge pick resolves to its **run** (one straight stretch or one arc), so an arc of a filleted rim works too. The fit reuses `feature_arc::fit_arc` and its tolerances, and checks every vertex. A non-circular edge is refused, never guessed. The axis sign is canonical, so a hole in a top face reads +Z. The centre is in the active setup's view frame (#326), the frame the WCS is set in.

**Command + MCP** - `SetWcsAtCircleCentre` (`crates/app/src/commands/wcs_circle.rs`) resolves the circle when the command is created and wraps `SetWcsOrigin` at the centre: one undo step, and undo restores the previous origin. The MCP tool `set_wcs_circle_centre { edge: {model, id}, rotation? }` (`crates/app/src/mcp/wcs_circle.rs`) runs the same command and returns the circle's centre, axis and diameter. The camcraft-mcp skill doc lists the tool. No MCP follow-up is needed.

**WCS page** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs`, split out of the 1894-line `pages.rs`):
- Three collapsible sections: *Origin and orientation*, *Quarter turns* and *Anchor on*.
- The six value fields sit in a two-column grid, label and field on one row, with the fields in one column.
- The quarter turns are two rows of three equal buttons ([X+ Y+ Z+] / [X- Y- Z-]), plus *Level* and *Set Origin* as two equal halves. Every row spans the pane's width.
- The anchor grid is a 3x3 compass of equal cells (up to 72 x 30), placed exactly and centred.
- *Anchor on* has a third choice, **Circle centre**. It shows a "Pick a circular edge" toggle and then the result, e.g. "Circle Ø 20.00 mm, centre (0.00, 0.00, 10.00)", or "Not anchored: <reason>". While the toggle is armed, a viewport click takes feature edges only, one run per click, and hover highlights what a click would take. A landed pick disarms the toggle. Choosing Circle centre disarms the box markers, and the other way round.
- The Bottom/Middle/Top radios are now a plain "Z level" row. Beside the 120 px label column they widened the section past a narrow pane.

**Plumbing** - `CommandKind::SetWcsCircle`, and a new `state_wcs.rs` that also takes over the existing `SetWcs` arm (`state.rs` shrinks). The viewport routes clicks through `wcs_pick.rs` (anchor markers + circle pick), which shortens `interact.rs`. `feature_click::ask` returns the circle ask while armed.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/circle_centre.rs` (new, 5 tests) uses a plate with a drilled 8 mm hole (32 chords), off-centre at (5, -3):
  - `a_drilled_hole_rim_gives_its_true_centre_axis_and_radius`: centre within 1e-6, Ø 8, axis +Z, through a real ray pick, and again with the part moved.
  - `a_straight_edge_is_refused_by_name`.
  - `an_elliptical_rim_and_a_face_are_refused_never_guessed`: ellipse gives `NotCircular`, face gives `NotAnEdge`, stale id gives `Gone`.
  - `the_anchor_command_places_the_origin_and_undo_restores_the_previous_one`: undo, redo, and a refusal never builds a command.
  - `mcp_set_wcs_circle_centre_anchors_on_a_rim_and_refuses_a_straight_edge`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page_tests.rs` (structural, no pixels):
  - `the_page_has_three_sections_and_one_row_fields_in_one_column`
  - `quarter_turns_are_equal_buttons_filling_the_pane`
  - `the_anchor_points_are_a_centred_compass_of_equal_cells`
  - It also holds the three `turn_wcs` tests, moved verbatim from `pages.rs`. The test count is unchanged.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_circle_tests.rs`:
  - `a_rim_click_anchors_the_origin_on_its_centre_and_undo_restores_it`: combo, then the pick button, then a viewport click on a boss rim, then G54 at the centre. The page states the circle, and Undo restores (1, 2, 3).
  - `a_face_is_refused_by_name_and_lands_nothing`
- Gate (macOS, worktree target):
  - Ran green: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `camcraft-app --lib`, the full `camcraft-ui` lib and integration suites (459 lib tests), and these app suites: circle_centre, feature_pick, feature_pick_wire, mcp, mcp_setup, mcp_pick, mcp_live, one_wcs, setup_wcs, commands_undo, wcs_align, wcs_view_pose, face_origin, vertex_pick, pick.
  - Not run: `cargo xtask gate quick` itself. Its dry run fell back to every crate, which is batch-sized.

## Not exercised

- Nobody has looked at the page in the real app (hand check below). No snapshot PNG changed. The release-lane `egui_shell_snapshot` was not run; the WCS page is not in that frame.
- A circle on a rotated or aligned setup is covered by the view-pose transform, and the app test covers a translated part. No rotated-setup test was added.

## Hand check

1. Open the WCS node and check the three sections. Each field should sit on one row with its label. Narrow the properties pane: the turn buttons should stretch evenly, and the compass should stay centred with equal cells.
2. Set *Anchor on: Circle centre*, then press *Pick a circular edge*. Hovering a hole rim or boss edge should highlight it. A click should move the WCS origin to the circle centre at the rim's height and show "Circle Ø … , centre (…)". Ctrl+Z should restore the previous origin.
3. With the pick armed, click a straight edge: the status line and the page should say it is straight, and the origin should stay put.
4. Switch back to Stock box: the compass and "Pick markers in viewport" should work as before.

title: build(xtask): cargo xtask package is the one Windows zip layout
body:
## What changed

One Windows zip layout instead of two, and the workflows/docs call `cargo xtask` directly (#752; maintainer: "We do not want double code and make this confusing.").

- **`cargo xtask package [--version X.Y.Z] [--out dist] [--bin-dir <dir>] [--dry-run]`** (new `xtask/src/package.rs`): stages `camcraft-<ver>-win-x64/` with the layout in `release_pack.rs` and writes `camcraft-<ver>-win-x64.zip`. No bump, no commit, no build. Without `--version` it reads `<bin-dir>/post.exe --version`, which is what the old workflow block did. Under Actions it appends `version=`, `stage=` and `zip=` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` and `CAMCRAFT_VERSION=` to `$GITHUB_ENV`.
  - Zip writer: still PowerShell `Compress-Archive`, with no new crate. It uses `pwsh` when that is on PATH, else Windows PowerShell 5.1. The runner has pwsh, which is the same tool the old step used.
  - Non-Windows: a real run is refused by name, since the zip is the win-x64 package and the other OSes ship from `package-*.sh`. `--dry-run` lists the tree on any host.
- **`cargo xtask release`**: its zip phase now calls `package::package`; the second copy of the staging/zip code is removed.
- **release.yml (Windows job)**: the inline "Assemble portable zip" PowerShell is replaced by `cargo xtask package --bin-dir target/release --out dist` (step id `zip` kept). The job output `version: ${{ steps.zip.outputs.version }}` and `CAMCRAFT_VERSION` keep their names. The installer step now passes `-Stage "${{ steps.zip.outputs.stage }}"`, which is the same directory as installer.ps1's default, now named explicitly. Build, signing, cert cleanup, uploads, triggers and the other jobs are unchanged.
- **ci.yml / nightly.yml**: `cargo xtask gate batch` / `cargo xtask gate release` (shell bash) replace `./scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier ...`. Triggers and matrices are unchanged (`workflow_dispatch` only), and the header comments are corrected.
- **scripts/README.md**: the gate section is rewritten around `cargo xtask gate`, with Windows and macOS/Linux examples. The wrappers are mentioned once. The "push/PR CI" / "nightly CI" wording is fixed, since both workflows are manual-only. There are new "Decisions" and "Portable zip (`cargo xtask package`)" sections, and the installer and signing text now name `cargo xtask release`.
- **Process files**: the AGENTS.md fork-sync list (prose and the `git checkout upstream/main -- ...` command) and review-prs step 2d now include `scripts/release.ps1` and `scripts/collect-decisions.ps1` / `.sh`. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` goes 8 -> 9. #681 is not posted (that happens at merge).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/752-xtask-package.md`.

## How tested

- `cargo test -p xtask`: 28 passed. New pinning tests in `xtask/src/release_tests.rs`:
  - `package_parse_takes_its_flags`
  - `package_dry_run_lists_the_release_yml_tree_on_any_host`

  - `package_reports_what_github_actions_steps_read`

  - The existing `zip_layout_mirrors_release_yml` still pins the staged file list.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run` plans exactly the xtask unit tests.
- **Layout evidence (old block vs xtask):** I ran the old workflow block's PowerShell body verbatim (with `$ver = "0.0.0"` and the post.exe/GITHUB_* lines removed) under Windows PowerShell 5.1. It ran in a temp folder holding copies of `assets/`, the four docs and fake `target/release/{camcraft-ui,camcraft-cli,post}.exe`. Then I ran `cargo xtask package --version 0.0.0 --bin-dir <that fake dir> --out <temp>/new` on this tree. Results:

title: build(xtask): cargo xtask release ports the release cut cross-platform
body:
## What changed

`cargo xtask release --version X.Y.Z --no-tag [--title T] [--skip-gate] [--skip-build] [--installer] [--dry-run]` ports `scripts/release.ps1`'s ten phases into xtask (`xtask/src/release.rs`, `release_bump.rs`, `release_pack.rs`, tests in `release_tests.rs`). `scripts/release.ps1` is now a thin wrapper forwarding its old switches. AGENTS.md (release step 2, the fix-only hand-test line) and `scripts/README.md` name `cargo xtask release`; `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` 7 -> 8. No new dependency (regex was already xtask's).

Per OS:
- **Windows**: as before - `sign.ps1` (phase 7), zip staged in Rust + `Compress-Archive` (phase 8), `installer.ps1` on `--installer` (phase 9).
- **Linux / macOS / FreeBSD**: phase 8 runs `scripts/package-linux.sh` / `package-macos.sh` / `package-freebsd.sh` (macOS builds both architectures in phase 5, as release.yml does); phase 7 is skipped by name; `--installer` is refused by name before phase 1. Any other OS is refused by name.

**Windows exe lock (#750 review):** the cut never builds the xtask package while it runs. The gate runs in process (`plan::release` through `exec::Run`, not a nested `cargo xtask gate release`, which would `cargo run -p xtask` and relink the running exe), and the release build names `-p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post` instead of the whole workspace (pinned by `release_build_never_builds_xtask`).

## Deliberate differences from release.ps1 (also in docs/decisions/749-xtask-release.md)
- Gate phase runs the current `gate release` tier (13 steps, incl. the ui snapshot lane) instead of the old script's own 6-command list.
- Build phase builds the product packages only (release.yml's list), not `cargo build --release` of the workspace.
- Cargo.lock: workspace path packages bumped in Rust, then still `cargo update -w -q` and the version-lines-only diff guard.
- Zip carries `NOTICE`, as release.yml's does (the old local script left it out); asset dirs copied recursively.
- No tag code path: the old script already refused every tagging run ("main is branch-protected"); same message kept. Commit messages and trailer kept verbatim.
- AGENTS.md's hand-test line said `release.ps1 -NoTag` "on main", which the script refuses; it now says a scratch branch off main.

- `cargo test -p xtask`: 23 passed (13 existing + 10 new). title: build(xtask): one cross-platform gate and decision collector
body:
Ports the gate and the decision collection into one cross-platform Rust tool, `cargo xtask`. Part of #748; the release port is split out to #749.

## What changed
- **New workspace member `xtask/`** (`publish = false`; alias `xtask = "run -p xtask --"` in `.cargo/config.toml`). 8 files, each under 300 lines, each with a provenance line. No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests.
  - `cargo xtask gate quick [--base main] [--heavy] | batch | release | test <filter> [--crate c] [--binary b] [--exact]`, and `--dry-run` (alias `--plan`) on any of them.
  - `cargo xtask decisions --version X.Y.Z`: the same output as collect-decisions.ps1, and it now rejects a version that isn't `X.Y.Z`.
- **It reproduces `gate.ps1`, not `gate.sh`.** That covers SLOW_BINARIES, the BATCH/ALL/SHARED/CLIPPY lists, `-j 6` / `--test-threads=6`, the ui CWD `crates/ui`, and quick's diff-to-test selection (changed `#[test]` fns run `--exact`; changed heavy fns are build-only unless `--heavy`; a suite edited outside its fns, or a new suite, runs whole; a src module runs the suites whose gate map names it, by submodule first; shared test input runs the crate's suites; geometry/cl/Cargo/.cargo/toolchain fall back to batch). It also covers the `gate-logs/<tier>-<timestamp>/` per-step logs, the failing-suite note, the summary table and the exit code. The gate drives `cargo test` / `cargo clippy` only and never launches or globs a test executable.
- **Wrappers.** `scripts/gate.ps1` (`-Tier`, `-Base`, `-Test`, `-Crate`, `-Binary`, `-Exact`, `-Heavy`, `-DryRun`), `scripts/gate.sh` (`quick [base]`, `batch`, `release`, `test <name> [crate] [--exact]`, `DRY_RUN=1`) and `scripts/collect-decisions.{ps1,sh}` are now thin forwarders. gate.sh accepts `--ignored` and drops it, because the gate reads `#[ignore]` from the source.
- **Process text.** AGENTS.md ("Three gate tiers", Actions budget, "Test the change", SLOW_BINARIES, release step 2, the decisions ledger, and the fork process-file list, which gains `xtask/` and `.cargo/config.toml`), the gate-runner and PR-reviewer agents, the review-prs / resolve-conflicts / work-issue skills, README and docs/decisions/README now name `cargo xtask gate ...` as the one command and say the wrappers still work. A fork whose tag predates xtask also adds the `"xtask"` member line in its sync commit; the AGENTS.md fork-sync text says so.
- **`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` 6 -> 7.** Not announced on #681: the merging session does that.
- **Decisions:** `docs/decisions/748-xtask-gate.md`.

**Deliberate differences from gate.ps1** (details in the decisions file):
1. `-Test` on a fn in a `tests/` module under `src/` (e.g. `ui/src/egui_app/tests/layout.rs`) was planned as `--test layout`, a suite that doesn't exist. It now runs as `--lib`.
2. Several lib files matching one filter gave duplicate `--lib` steps. They now share one step.
3. The heavy-fn hint text names `--heavy` / `gate test <name>`.
4. A change under `xtask/` runs xtask's unit tests in quick.
5. The log-dir timestamp is UTC.
6. Hashtable-ordered groups are now sorted.

**New dependency (for `needs-maintainer`):** `regex = "1"` in xtask only. It is already in `Cargo.lock` (pulled in by tracing-subscriber's env-filter), so no new crate enters the tree; the lock gains only the `xtask` package entry. It lets the gate-map, test-fn-span and diff-hunk patterns port one-for-one from gate.ps1's .NET regexes. serde_json isn't needed, because there's no artifact list to parse (the gate never runs test exes itself).

**Release: not ported.** `scripts/release.ps1` (243 lines, 10 phases, zip + installer + signing) stays as it is. Follow-up: #749 ("xtask release: port scripts/release.ps1 cross-platform", Part of #748). That's why this PR says `Refs #748`, not `Fixes`.

## How tested (Windows 11 only)
- `cargo test -p xtask`: 13 unit tests pass. They pin the plan selection on a throwaway fixture workspace (changed files -> planned steps):
  - `changed_test_fn_runs_exact_and_heavy_fn_only_builds`
  - `suite_edit_outside_fns_and_new_suite_run_whole`
  - `src_module_maps_to_gate_mapped_suites`
  - `shared_test_input_runs_every_suite_of_the_crate`
  - `manifest_or_shared_crate_falls_back_to_batch`
  - `nothing_in_crates_plans_nothing_and_xtask_runs_its_own_tests`
  - `batch_skips_slow_binaries_and_release_runs_everything`
  - `slow_list_is_pinned`
  - `single_test_finds_suite_and_lib_fns`
  - `test_fn_spans_cover_attrs_through_closing_brace`
  - `cli_parses_the_gate_forms`
  - `decisions_gathered_in_issue_order_and_removed`
  - `log_names_stamps_and_notes_match_the_old_script`
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- **Parity, `--dry-run` against origin/main's `scripts/gate.ps1 -DryRun`, same tree.** The summary/wall lines were stripped and the outputs diffed.
  - `batch`: **identical** (31 lines).
  - `release`: **identical** (43 lines).
  - `quick` on a 6-file sample diff (a scratch worktree at origin/main): one changed fn in `app/tests/arcs.rs`, one changed `#[ignore]`d fn in `app/tests/operations.rs`, `app/src/posting.rs`, `motion/src/machining2d/arcs.rs`, the header line of `sim/tests/arc_plane.rs`, and a new untracked `tools/tests/parity_new.rs`. Result: 6 steps, all identical (tools new suite; sim whole suite; motion `--lib` + 33 gate-mapped suites; app `--lib` + 81 gate-mapped suites; app build-only `operations`; app `arcs` 1 fn `--exact`) and all plan notes identical. The only differences: git's CRLF warnings, which the old script let through, and the reworded `--heavy` hint (item 3 above).
  - `-Test` forms: identical for `fitted_arcs_recover_a_bore_rim -Exact`, `the_ramp_flag -Crate app` (ignored -> release), `tool_kind -Crate tools`, `-Binary nope` (no match, exit 1) and `structural`. `the_viewport_tab_is_permanent -Exact` differs on purpose (item 1): old `--test layout` (no such suite), new `--lib`.
  - Wrappers: `gate.ps1 -Tier batch -DryRun` gives output identical to `cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run`. `gate.ps1 -Test ... -Crate tools -Exact -DryRun`, `DRY_RUN=1 gate.sh test ... tools --exact`, `gate.sh release` (13 steps) and `gate.sh quick origin/main` produce the expected plans. `collect-decisions.sh 1.2` is refused (exit 2).
- **Real run end to end:** `cargo xtask gate test tools_bin_lists_a_sane_catalog --crate tools --exact` built and ran `camcraft-tools --test headless_bin -- --exact ...`: 1 passed, log written, summary printed, exit 0.

## Not exercised
- **macOS and Linux were not exercised**: this machine runs Windows only. The code uses `Path`/`PathBuf`, `CARGO` from the environment, and no `.exe` or drive assumptions, and `gate.sh` is plain bash 3.2. It still needs one run on each OS.
- A real `quick`/`batch`/`release` run (only dry runs plus the one real test step). This PR's own quick falls back to batch (manifest change), and a full batch wasn't run, as briefed.
- `cargo xtask decisions` against the real `docs/decisions/` (it would consume the files). The fixture unit test covers it.

title: docs(process): weight every issue by effort and route it to a matching worker agent
body:
Draft for the maintainer's review (2026-11-10: "we need a way of 'weighting' an issue ... launched with the matching agent - this to manage token spend on different levels of complexity of tickets").

## What changes
- **AGENTS.md, Issue Law: new "Every issue is weighted by effort".**
  - **Labels:** one `effort:low|medium|high|max` label per issue, beside `P*`, rating the *work*, not a model. A table gives the examples.
  - **When it's set:** at filing. A human-filed issue gets one at its first triage.
  - **Safety floor:** anything that can change posted G-code, a collision or gouge check, stock simulation or geometry is at least `effort:high`, and so is every P0.
  - **Who works it:** `P*` still decides *what* is worked next, and `effort:*` decides *who* works it. The main session dispatches the issue to `.claude/agents/issue-worker-<effort>.md` and keeps the review and merge decisions.
  - **Review tier:** reviews run at least on the medium tier, and on high for anything under the safety floor.
  - **Escalation:** a worker that fails its quick gate twice, or finds the work bigger than its label, stops. It comments what it learned, raises the label one step and releases the claim. One escalation per run; only the maintainer lowers a label.
  - **The other label lists:** `needs-research` sub-issues, follow-up issues and agent-filed issues now include `effort:*`.
- **`.claude/agents/issue-worker-{low,medium,high,max}.md`:** four thin agents. Their only difference is `model:` (haiku / sonnet / opus / fable) and which labels they accept. The model choice lives only here, so a fork on other models edits four lines. A 404 on a model alias means running without `model:` and saying so in the claim comment.
- **`.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md`:** the shared worker procedure.
  - **Pre-checks:** `P?`, needs-research, blocked, a live claim, or an effort above the worker's tier mean it stops.
  - **Steps:** claim, then a worktree from the latest main, then the fix with a pinning test, then the quick gate.
  - **Escalation:** the rule above.
  - **Finish:** a draft PR with an `Effort:` line, the issue moved to `in-review`, and the worktree removed. It never merges, never marks the PR ready and never reviews its own work.
- **`.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md` step 2c:** the cost comment adds `Effort: <label>` and any escalation, the data for recalibrating the table.
- **`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`:** 5 → 6.

## Not in this PR (after merge)
- **Labels:** create `effort:low`, `effort:medium`, `effort:high` and `effort:max`.
- **Tagging pass:** one pass over the open issues proposes and applies an effort label to each from the table, as a separate step the maintainer can correct.
- **Announcement:** a `PROCESS_VERSION 6` note on #681.
- **gh-issues skill:** the local skill (outside the repo) gets the same filing rule.

## Open questions for review
- **Tier mapping:** low=Haiku is the lowest bar. On this codebase I expect it to fit only truly mechanical issues. Keep it, or start `low` on Sonnet?
- **Safety floor:** high is the proposed level. Should it be `max` for collision and gouge laws?
- **Escalation trigger:** "two failed quick gates" is a guess. The cost data will show whether it's right.

title: fix(ui,app): setup alignment composes on the current pose, one flow, readable picks (#738)
body:
## What changed (#738, maintainer-reported, P1)

1. **Moves compose on the current pose.** Laying on a face or on three points now computes the lay in the setup's current alignment and composes it onto that alignment, through new `pick::lay_on_plane_in` / `lay_on_points_in` and `setup_turn::held_centre`. Before, each move went back to the import pose first. Axes already composed. Each move is still one `AlignPartToSetup`, and one undo returns to the previous pose exactly. Re-applying the same pick is a zero step and is refused as "already holds the part that way".
2. **One flow.** The top row now reads "Part alignment - each move starts from where the part sits now", and its tooltip describes the flow.
   - "Start from a preset" presets turn the part from where it sits, and so does the typed "Turn by", through the new `CommandKind::TurnPart` → `AlignPartToSetup::turn_by`.
   - "As modelled" is the one reset.
   - The pickers' Apply tooltips say a move starts from the current pose and is one undo step.
3. **Readable status.** It now reads "1 face selected", "2 points selected" or "1 edge selected" (`pick_words`).
   - Points show where they are: "Point 2: on 'part' (x, y, z) mm".
   - Internal ids ("Face 0xccc7c…") never show; app refusals on the page are stripped of " 0x…".
4. **Picks you can see.** `align_pick_viz::paint`:
   - picked faces are filled with the pick violet (alpha 96);
   - picked points are 6 px filled discs;
   - picked edges are 4 px strokes.

**Splits, so no large file grows:**
- `commands/align_stock.rs` comes out of `setup_align.rs` (422 → 298 lines).
- `state_align.rs` comes out of `state.rs` (4116 → 4062 lines).
- No snapshot PNG changed.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/738-align-flow.md`.

## Pinned by
- `align_compose` (new, 3 tests):
  - axes then face;
  - face then three points;
  - turn-by after a lay, for both pivots, plus the zero and NaN refusals.

  Each checks that the second move composes on the first, and that undo, undo and redo step back exactly.
- `setup_align_tests::a_preset_after_a_face_lay_composes_and_as_modelled_is_the_one_reset` (real clicks, Ctrl+Z).
- `setup_plane_tests::the_pick_status_counts_the_face_and_never_shows_an_id` and `setup_points_tests::the_pick_status_counts_the_points_and_never_shows_an_id`.
- `plane_face_pick::picked_faces_fill_points_are_discs_and_edges_are_bold` (paint assertions on the rendered shell).
- `pick_words` unit tests.

## Tested
- **app suites:** all green. lib 107, `align_compose` 3, `plane_align` 9, `plane_align_edges` 5, `points_align` 8, `axis_align` 10, `setup_align` 9, `turn_pivot` 5, `commands_undo` 32, `project_roundtrip` 71, `wcs_align` 5, `mcp_setup` 6, `fixture_locate` 11, `winding_align` 9, `setup_carry` 9, `setup_relative` 9, `setup_stock_source` 6, `fixture_locate_stock` 3, `wcs_view_pose` 3.
- **ui suites:** all green, lib 447.
- **clippy `-D warnings`:** ui lib+tests and the app lib are clean.

## Not exercised / for the hand check
- The look of the fill, discs and bold edges on a real part, including a tilted face.
- How the new wording reads in the narrow properties pane.
- Pressing "Turn by" Apply twice turns the part twice; this is intended.
- **Behaviour change:** MCP `lay_part_on_points` / `lay_part_on_plane` now also compose, since they share the command.

**Stays a draft until the maintainer or user hand-checks it** (binary: `~/camcraft-builds/camcraft-ui-738`).

Fixes #738

title: feat(machines): Sienci AltMill 2x4, 4x4 and 4x8 on the grblHAL post
body:
**Stacked on #715** (grblHAL post, not merged yet): this branch is #715's head plus one commit, so the diff shows #715's files too until it merges. Only commit `feat(machines): Sienci AltMill ...` is this PR. Fork synced at v0.16.0 (via #715's base).

## What changed

Three built-in machines for Sienci's AltMill routers, which run grblHAL on the SLB-EXT controller. They post through the existing `grblhal.cps`; there is no AltMill post file.

- `assets/machines/sienci-altmill-2x4.mch`, `-4x4.mch` and `-4x8.mch`, registered in `posting::MACHINES` as "Sienci AltMill 2x4", "4x4" and "4x8".
- **Units mm, 3 axes.** The Vortex rotary waits on #714.
- **`safe_retract: 0.0`.** The AltMill homes (`$22=79`: homing on, required at startup, machine origin 0 at home; Z homes up; soft limits on). So every tool change lifts `G53 G0 Z0`, then `T<n> M6` stands alone. gSender and ncSender take over on `T<n> M6` (manual change, RapidChange or Sienci ATC), so the post needs no ATC or manual mode and no rack list.
- **Figures** from Sienci's spec pages. The 4x4's travel (1260 x 1248 x 170 mm soft limits), axis rates and spindle range (1200-24000 rpm) are read from a 4x4's own `$$`. Every figure and its source is in `docs/decisions/728-altmill.md`.

## How tested

- New `altmill_machines.rs` (4 tests): each file's figures; the `G53 G0 Z0` lift before each `T<n> M6` and no G43/G43.1/G49; a spindle speed past 24000 refused; the 4x4 two-tool program locked byte-exact in mm and inch (`golden/nc/grblhal/altmill_4x4_two_tool{,_inch}.nc`).
- Green on macOS: `altmill_machines`, `machine` (the library list now pins the three), `machine_library`, `machine_edit`, `conformance`, `grblhal_post`, `tormach_machines`. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test altmill_machines -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No run on the machine yet. The owner has an AltMill 4x4 with an SLB-EXT, an 8-pocket RapidChange ATC and ncSender, and will report an air-cut of the 4x4 golden here.
- The 2x4 and 4x8 figures come from Sienci's pages only; an owner's `$$` would confirm them.
- Full workspace gate not run (disk-limited machine); the suites above are the ones that touch the machine registry and the grblHAL post.

title: docs(process): the camcraft-mcp skill's tool signatures match the server
body:
**Fixes #724.** The `camcraft-mcp` skill told agents argument names the server refuses, for 8 tools. This corrects them, brings the gap list current, and adds a test so the skill can't drift from `tools/list` silently again.

**Process change:** `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` is a process file, so `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` goes 4 -> 5. A suggested #681 line for the merging session:

> **PROCESS_VERSION 5** · PR #(this) · the `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool signatures now match the server (`post` takes `output`, `add_operation` takes `source`, `set_stock` takes `box {dx, dy, dz}` / `cylinder` / `from_model`, `set_operation_area` / `set_operation_geometry` take `operation`, `set_work_offset` takes `word`, `load_machine` takes `builtin` / `path` / `clear`, `add_tool` takes `catalog`), and its gap list is current. **Fork action:** pull the process files; an agent that learned the old names should use the new ones.

### What changed

- **`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, the tool reference:** the 8 drifted entries now use the names the server publishes. The list is in #724.
- **`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, "Known Remaining Gaps":**
  - Moved to "shipped": pocket recognition (#35, `detect_pockets`), in-plane part axes (#557, `set_part_axes`), and the live GUI session (#183, #567, `--mcp-port` / `mcp --connect`). Also three-point alignment (#555, `lay_part_on_points`) and the fixture locate (#561, `locate_part`), which merged while this PR was open (3961e031).
  - `MoveModel` and `RepairModel` now point to their open PRs, #719 and #721.
  - Face-to-plane alignment (#330) is noted as GUI-only.
- **`crates/app/tests/mcp_skill_signatures.rs` (new), the drift alarm:** for every `` - `name { … }` `` signature in the skill, the tool must exist, each top-level documented key must be an `inputSchema` property, and each required argument must be documented.
  - A floor on how many signatures it finds (30; the skill has 34) keeps a format change from making it pass on nothing.
  - `the_key_reader_takes_top_level_keys_only` pins the small parser itself: quoted values and nested object fields aren't arguments.
- **`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`:** 4 -> 5.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/724-mcp-skill-signatures.md`.

No product code changes.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

Fork: `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, `main` at upstream f42d3788 (contains v0.16.0, PROCESS_VERSION 4). Gated on 47a7d0e7.

The other 2 of the 8 (`set_stock`, `add_tool`) were wrong in their prose, which the test doesn't read.

title: fix(app): verify's ok is false while an op's own warnings hold the post
body:
**Fixes #722.** `verify` said `"ok": true` for a program whose post was then refused by the ops' own warnings. So `camcraft-cli process <project>` (no `-o`) exited 0, "clean", for a job it couldn't post.

### What changed

- **`crates/app/src/script/api.rs`, `v_verify`:** behind `cam.verify`, `cam.check` and the MCP `verify` tool, and through them the CLI's exit code.
  - `ok` now also requires that no op in scope holds the post with its own cached warnings.
  - The rule is the post's own, in the new `holds_post`: a suppressed op is not in the program, and a warning counts exactly when `Warning::blocks_post()` is true. That is when `posting::stream_records` writes it as a `WARN` record, and any `WARN` record refuses the post. A Scallop or ProbeSearch note still doesn't count.
  - The report gains `held_by`: the labels of the ops in scope holding the post, empty when none.
- **`assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` and its template in `crates/app/src/script/mod.rs`:** `VerifyReport` documents `ok` and the new `held_by` (the bindings drift test keeps the two equal).
- **`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`:** the `verify` tool's description says what `ok` and `held_by` mean.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/722-verify-ok-warnings.md`.

What stays the same: the program gate (`posting::verification_report`), the post's refusal text, and the findings list. Only the summary now agrees with them.

**Behaviour change, intended:** `camcraft-cli process <project>` without `-o` now exits 1 ("the job is not clean") for a job whose ops' warnings would refuse the post. Before, it exited 0.

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/mcp_verify.rs`, new)

The fixture is a real collision. `EM-0400-2FL` is a Ø4 cutter with 12 mm of flute on a Ø6 shank, so contouring a 30 mm wall rubs the shank on the part below the flutes (84 `shank_hit` findings). A 10 mm wall stays inside the flutes and is clean.

- `verify_is_not_ok_while_an_ops_own_warnings_hold_the_post`: the 30 mm job has a fresh op and a passing gate, and every finding blocks the post. `ok` is `false`, `held_by` is `["C1"]` (the same answer for `verify {name: "C1"}`), and the post is still refused with "warning(s)".
- `a_contour_inside_the_flutes_still_verifies_ok_and_posts`: the 10 mm neighbour has no findings, `ok: true`, `held_by: []`, and the post writes.
- `the_cli_process_lane_exits_one_for_a_job_its_warnings_hold`: both jobs saved as projects and run through the real `camcraft-cli process`. The 30 mm job exits 1 with "not clean", the 10 mm job exits 0.

With `api.rs` put back to `main`, all three fail. The first fails at `a program the post refuses is not ok`, and the CLI test because the held job exits 0. The neighbour fails too, but only because `held_by` is a new key.

title: feat(post): grblHAL post processor (3-axis mill)
body:
Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## What changed

A new built-in post, **grblHAL** (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, 3-axis mill), and a generic machine, **grblHAL 3-axis** (`assets/machines/grblhal-3axis.mch`). The post is specced from the G-code list in grblHAL's public core README and the LinuxCNC G-code reference (behaviour only; grblHAL's GPL source was not read), structured after `tormach.cps`.

- Header `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G80`; no `%`, O word, N numbers or G64.
- **No tool length word** (no G43 / G43.1 / G49): on grblHAL the offset belongs to the controller's tool-change handling, and a G49 would discard a measured length. This departs from the issue's G43.1 default; reasoning in `docs/decisions/710-grblhal-post.md`.
- `G53 G0 Z<safe>` then `T<n> M6` **alone on its line**; no G28/G30.
- Canned cycles G73/G81/G82/G83/G86/G89 with G98, dwell P in seconds.
- Refused by name: control/wear compensation (G41/G42), tapping (G84), going home after an operation (G28/G30 positions are controller settings), tilted moves, and probing (the engine refuses it, since the post has no probe hooks).
- **Z lift without trusting an unhomed machine Z0.** With `$22=0` grblHAL takes its power-on position as machine zero, so `G53 G0 Z0` could rapid down. `G53 G0 Z<safe>` is written only when the machine file states `safe_retract` (= "it homes"). Otherwise the lift is `G0 Z<h>` in the work offset, where h is the section's `ClearancePlane` or a higher Z already commanded; it is refused by name when h is unknown or not above `StockZTop`. The generic machine states no `safe_retract`.

## How tested

- `conformance`: grblHAL in POSTS / REFUSED (`tap_plate`, "tapping") / EXTENSIONS. Goldens in `golden/nc/grblhal/` (12) and `golden/nc/synth_grblhal.nc`. The synth stream drops only the tap.
- New `grblhal_post.rs` (9 tests): registry and library, grbl program shape with no length/G64/G28/G30/G84 word, Z lift before a lone `T M6`, dwell P1.5 for 1500 ms, one named tap refusal, inch output, a homed machine lifting with G53, the work-offset lift without homing (clearance, a higher commanded Z, origin shift), and the named refusal of an unknown or buried lift height.
- Cross-post lists extended: `comment_escape`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `post/tests/comp`, `fanuc_post` (non-RTCP; the tilt refusal is now looked for among all warnings, since grblHAL also refuses its lift on that bare stream), `inverted_post`, `after_op` (stops plus the home refusal), `coolant`, `coolant_followups`, `machine` (library expectations).

Quick gate (debug) on the final tree: 28 camcraft-app binaries, among them conformance 6 (goldens unchanged by the lift fix, their machine states safeRetractZ 0), grblhal_post 9, fanuc_post 11, after_op 10, coolant 7, machine 32 and posting 17, all green; camcraft-post `comp` 9/9; camcraft-ui lib `machines_pane` 6/6 and `post` 19/19; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib -- -D warnings` clean. Whole-crate `clippy --tests` stops on the pre-existing `lathe_thread_travel.rs:83` compile error (missing field `hand`), which is on upstream main and not touched here.

## Not exercised

**Not yet run on a real grblHAL controller or its simulator - testers welcome.** Anyone with a grblHAL machine: please post a program with this post, dry-run it (no stock, Z raised, hand on feed hold), and report on #710, especially the Z lift before each tool change and at the end. The Setup pane's End-units row still appears only for Tormach, although the script reads `EndUnits`.

Changelog: grblHAL post processor (3-axis mill) and a generic grblHAL 3-axis machine; G41/G42, G84, probing and go-home are refused by name

Fixes #710

title: fix(app): the program sim sweeps a tap at its thread's minor diameter
body:
**Replaces #271**, which closed itself on 2026-11-10 when its branch was pushed: the old fork `austin62jake/Camcraft` had left this repo's fork network, so GitHub could no longer follow its head. Same commits, now from the new fork `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, with `main` f42d3788 merged in (no conflicts). The review history and mkinney's conflict notes are on #271.

Fork: `austin62jake/Camcraft2`, created 2026-11-10 from upstream `main` f42d3788 (contains v0.16.0, PROCESS_VERSION 4).

**Partial fix for #266.** This removes one of the two checks that refuse a tap on a normally modelled hole. The other one still blocks the post; see "What is left" below.

### What changed

- The program sim (the stock-sim clause of the post gate) swept a Tap-kind tool at its full major diameter. CAD models a tapped hole at the thread's minor (tap-drill) size, and a tap only cuts the thread band outside that wall. So the sim read the band as a gouge down the whole hole wall and refused the post.
- A Tap-kind tool now sweeps its thread's core: `diameter / 2 - 0.5413 x pitch`. That is the ISO 724 radial thread depth, the same constant the thread-mill generator already uses (`machining2d::THREAD_DEPTH_PER_PITCH`). For M6 x 1 the core is Ø4.917.
- The rule lives in one place, `operation::tool_law::cutting_radius`, so a later fix to the generator's verify can read the same number. Every other tool still sweeps half its diameter. A pitch too coarse to leave a core is refused by name.
- A tap over a hole smaller than its core, or over solid metal, is still a gouge.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/266-tap-minor-sweep.md`.

### Readings

| Case (M6 x 1 tap, plate with a blind hole) | Program sim before | Program sim after |
|---|---|---|
| Ø5 hole (tap drill) | gouge, worst 12.000 mm on the hole wall | clean, 0 gouge cells |
| Ø3 hole (too small) | gouge | gouge (still refused) |

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/tap_sim.rs`)

- `a_tap_in_a_hole_modelled_at_tap_drill_size_is_not_a_gouge`: fails on `main` (`worst 12.000 mm at (-0.31, -2.94, z 8.0)`), passes with the fix.
- `a_tap_wider_than_its_hole_is_still_a_gouge`: guards the other side; passes before and after.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

**On this head (9410e5ba, `main` f42d3788 merged), Windows 10:**

- The quick gate's plan (`scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick -DryRun`, run by hand at `-j 4`): app lib 103 passed, plus 24 suites, 130 passed: `carried_fixtures_cache` 6, `carried_verify` 8, `contour_arc_sim` 1, `edge_break_bound` 3, `edge_break_gate` 5, `lathe_field_sim` 6, `lathe_field_tools` 2, `post_not_judged` 4, `posting` 17, `probe_only_sim` 2, `real_tip_contour` 4, `rotary_field_parity` 3, `setup_align` 9, `setup_carry` 9, `setup_stock_source` 6, `stock_engine_agreement` 0, `stock_export` 2, `stock_field_cost` 0, `stock_sim_document` 9, `stock_view` 4, `tap_sim` 2, `tool_law` 4, `verify` 21, `wall_column_gouge` 3. 7 are `#[ignore]`d in the source (`rotary_field_parity` 1, `stock_engine_agreement` 3, `stock_field_cost` 1, `verify` 2). No failures.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**On the earlier heads (#271):**


- Both pinning tests alone, with the fix, and with `stock_sim.rs` put back to `main` (the first one fails there as above).
- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick`: app lib plus 13 suites (the gate map's `stock_sim` and `tool_law` suites plus `tap_sim`), 155 tests, all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The app, through `camcraft-cli mcp`, built from this branch (upstream `main` 897a820 plus this commit): imported a plate STL with a round Ø5 blind hole, added `TAP-M6` and a Drill/Tap op, generated, verified. The program gate now reports `ok` with no problems. With a Ø3 hole it still reports `gouge: program cuts below the model in 127 cell(s), worst 6.00 mm`.
- Baseline batch tier on clean `main` 897a820 on this machine: all suites pass except three UI pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`), which also fail without this change. Not run on Linux or macOS.

### What is left (why this is `Refs`, not `Fixes`)

With this fix the Ø5 tap job still does not post. The op's own verify flags `move 1 cuts past the finish surface` and `move 2 cuts past the finish surface` (the tap feeding in and out). That verify hands one tool radius (`tool.geom()`) to every law, including the rapids laws, where a tap's full diameter is the right envelope: a tap must never rapid into the thread band. I tried shrinking only the containment solid law's cutter; the tangency law still flags the same two moves, so I dropped that. Fixing it means splitting the cutting radius from the rapid envelope in the verifier's inputs, and it meets the convention in `solid_law_goldens.rs` that a tapped hole is modelled at the tap's major diameter. I left that for you to decide on the issue.

## What changed (step 2 of #692)
Every viewport picker and the MCP pick tools now resolve through #705's one pick rule. No page carries its own pick logic.

### The UI router: `crates/ui/src/feature_click.rs` (new)
- It builds the `PickRay` from the camera, in perspective or ortho.
- It converts the pixel radius to mm by depth.
- It says which kinds the armed tool accepts:

| Tool | Accepts |
|---|---|
| Plane row | faces only (#554) |
| Axis by edge | edges |
| Axis by two points | points |
| Operation geometry | Face, Edge (with the face between edges) or Vertex mode |
| Boundary | faces or edges |

- **Hover** uses exactly the rule its click would.
- **Origin/WCS chips** read the operation picks, so they get the same rule.

### Removed from the UI
- **`interact.rs`:** `pick_face`, `pick_edge`, `hover_feature_at`, `edge_nearest`, `point_seg_dist_px` and `feature_of_facet`. The old edge pick was screen-space, with no depth test, and offered facet seams. The file drops from 1779 to 1542 lines.
- **`vertex_pick.rs`:** its local nearest/sight logic. It drops from 271 to 122 lines.

### App side
- **`pick/feature_sel.rs` (new):** maps a pick to the `FeatureSel` the pages store (`Chain`, run or `Segment`). `check_pickable` refuses a pick by id that a click could never make.
- **MCP `list_features`:** now lists only feature-edge chains and feature points.
- **Graph cache:** cached per facet allocation, so hover never re-hashes a mesh.
- **Occlusion:** capped at 32 sight rays per candidate tier, a choice measured on `sample_ap214`.

### Intended behaviour changes (#692's rule)
- Rim vertices of round holes and bosses are no longer pickable points.
- Facet seams of smooth walls are no longer edges.
- Hidden edges are no longer pickable.
- In the feature modes, the stock-mesh hover triangle gives way to the feature highlight.

## What changed

**Machines.** `assets/machines/makera-carvera.mch` and `makera-carvera-air.mch` are new, registered in `posting::MACHINES`. The figures come from the "Specs" tables on Makera's own product pages (read 2026-11-10):

| | Carvera (C1) | Carvera Air |
|---|---|---|
| Work area (mm), as ±stroke | 360 × 240 × 140 | 300 × 200 × 130 |
| Spindle | 200 W, to 15000 rpm | 200 W, to 13000 rpm |
| Axis feed and rapid | 6000 mm/min | 4000 mm/min |
| Tool changer | 6 | none stated (quick changer) |
| Coolant | Air (M7) | Air (M7) |

No `min_speed` is stated, because Makera publishes "0 – 15000 rpm" and the validator refuses 0. The optional 4th-axis module is left out; it's a later step.

**Post.** `assets/posts/carvera.cps` is registered as "Makera Carvera". It writes only words from the firmware's supported-codes tables (Smoothieware-based).

| Area | What it writes |
|---|---|
| Header | `G21 G17 G90 G94`. An inch machine is refused by name, because G20 halts the firmware. |
| Tool change | `M6 Tn`. There's no G43, because the firmware measures tool length itself. Tool 0 (the wireless probe) is refused as a cutter. |
| Spindle and air | `M3 S…`, then the machine's M7 air, off with M9. |
| Arcs | `G2`/`G3` with relative I/J/K, in G17, G18 or G19. |

body:
## What changed (step 1 of #692)
This adds one app-layer picking service. Step 2 (a separate PR) moves every UI picker and the MCP pick tools onto it. No picker uses it yet, so app behaviour is unchanged.

### New modules
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_graph.rs` (330):** the feature graph of a mesh.
  - Welded faces are the existing `geometry::feature` patches, reused through `model::features_of_local`. `list_features` is unchanged.
  - Feature edges are creases between welded faces, plus open boundary edges. Seams between the strips of a tessellated wall are filtered out.
  - Feature points are corners (3 or more edges meet), turns over 30° and chain ends.
  - The graph has a cap-8 cache keyed by the facets' digest.
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_arc.rs` (90):** circle and arc centres of round feature-edge runs.
- **`crates/app/src/pick/feature_pick.rs` (314):** the one pick API, `pick_feature(world, &PickQuery { ray, radius, kinds, through }, skip)`, with `pick_bodies` for world-free callers.
  - It finds the front-most surface, then snaps point → centre → edge → face, only among the accepted kinds.
  - Edges and points must be visible from the eye: a perspective view checks the sight line, an ortho view the parallel view line. `through = true` turns the occlusion check off.
- **`pick.rs`:** registers the new modules; `ray_triangle` becomes `pub(crate)` so the new code shares it.

The thresholds and the alternatives dropped are in `docs/decisions/692-pick-graph.md`.

body:
**Stacked on #676** (#670, plasma profile), which is stacked on #674 (#669, plasma kind). Review only this PR's own commit, `2645a023`.

A **PathPilot plasma post for the Tormach 1300PL** (#671). Every word below was checked against UM10720 v1223A ([UM]) or Tormach's PathPilot Post Processor Guidelines, Plasma column ([PG]).

| Word | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `G20`/`G21` | units | [PG] |
| `G90 G91.1 G94 G17 G40 G49 G80` | modal reset, once | [PG]; [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G64 P0.005 Q0.005` | path blending (P in inches even under G21) | [UM] §6.2.1 p.50; [PG] |
| `G54` | work offset | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `G43 H1` | torch length offset | [PG] ("always H1"); [UM] §6.2.2 |
| `G30` | go to the G30 height | [UM] §6.2.1-6.2.2 |
| `G0 X Y` | rapid to the pierce point, never Z | [UM] §6.2.1 |
| `M200` | AutoFS (feed, THC volts, pierce height and delay, amps) | [UM] §6.3 p.51, §7.2 p.54 |
| `M207`/`M208`/`M209 P` | pierce height / cut height / pierce delay, only when the op states them | [UM] §6.3.1 p.52, §7.2 |
| `G15` | ohmic probe; WCS Z = 0 | [UM] §7.1 p.54 |
| `G16` | rise to pierce height, fire, delay, go to cut height, THC on | [UM] §7.1; [PG] |
| `G1/G2/G3 X Y [I J] [F]` | the cut, XY only | [PG] |
| `G41.1`/`G42.1 D<kerf>` … `G40` | control compensation, each on its own line before a straight lead | [PG] |
| `M205` | torch off, Z to the G30 height | [UM] §7.2 |
| `M30` | end | [PG] |

- **Never written:** S, M3-M9, M6, G95-G99, canned cycles.
- **M6 conflict:** [PG] says M6 is unsupported on plasma, but [UM]'s test program writes `T1 M6`. This follows the issue and [PG]; the conflict is recorded.

## What changed
- **Script:** `assets/posts/tormach-plasma.cps`, registered as "Tormach PathPilot Plasma", the only `PLASMA_POSTS` entry. Milling posts decline a plasma stream, because they lack the torch hooks.
- **Stream:** #676's records are carried into the post stream: `PLASMA …`, `TORCH ON C<id> …` and `TORCH OFF C<id>` (the `.cl` v5 records without `; `).
  - The parser reads both spellings; malformed records are refused by line number.
  - New properties: `PlasmaKerf`, `PlasmaCompensation`, `PierceHeight`, `CutHeight`, `PierceDelay` (absent = AutoFS), `PlasmaFeed`, `PlasmaReversed`, `Contour`, `ContourRole`, `ParentContour`, `SmallHole`.
  - New hooks: `onPlasma`, `onTorchOn`, `onTorchOff`.
  - `machine.kind` is now a script property.
- **Engine torch law** (`cnc_torch.rs`), refused by name:
  - a TORCH with no header, a second header;
  - ON while lit, a wrong or extra OFF, a rapid while lit;
  - a section or stream left lit;
  - a script without both torch hooks.
- **Post refusals:**
  - a non-plasma op, a Plasma Profile path with no plasma record;
  - rpm, coolant (other than off), a rotary or tilted move;
  - Z on a lit move, a canned cycle, a dark feed;
  - comp under a computer offset, wear comp;

- **AutoFS:** under AUTOFEED, no F is written. A small hole then runs at the AutoFS feed, with an operator comment; refusing it would block every default plate with a hole.

title: feat(ui): viewport origin gizmos wear their names (#727)
body:
With several setups on screen, every origin triad looks alike - nothing in the viewport says whose zero is whose (#727).

## The change

Every origin gizmo now labels itself at its origin. Each work-offset triad draws the entity name the Setup pane already uses (`G54` for the first setup, `Setup2/WCS` for the second) in bright triad blue at the ordinary overlay-label size; the dimmed world axes draw `World` in neutral gray dimmed by `WORLD_DIM`, like the lines under them. `Gizmo` (`interact.rs`) grows one `name` field, filled in `gizmos()` - which already honors the Models pane's eye (`hidden_offsets`) and the `show_world_axes` gate, so a hidden offset loses its name with its lines for free. `overlay_labels` places each name just below the projected origin (`NAME_DROP_UV = 0.02`, same currency as `axis_note::NOTE_DROP_UV`), emitted before the gizmo's `X`/`Y`/`Z` tips. Only the letters keep the big `is_axis_label` font. Rationale in `docs/decisions/727-viewport-gizmo-labels.md`.

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

- `gizmo_tests::the_dimmed_world_axes_are_labelled_world` - the fresh world's set carries `World`, neutral gray (equal channels) and dimmed like the axes.
- `gizmo_tests::each_triad_is_labelled_with_its_own_offset_name` - two setups: both `G54` and `Setup2/WCS` label their own origins, bright against the letters.
- `gizmo_tests::an_offset_name_stands_at_its_origin_not_its_axis_tips` - the name rides the projected origin horizontally, a small uv drop below it, not crowded onto the tips.
- `gizmo_tests::a_hidden_work_offset_drops_its_name_with_its_gizmo` - the pane's eye and the label agree.
- `gizmo_tests::gizmo_names_are_not_the_big_axis_letters` - `is_axis_label` still answers only X/Y/Z.
- Re-pins: label counts 3→4 (fresh world), 6→8 (two gizmos), 3→4 (moved origin); `axis_note_tests`' fresh-world set pins exactly `["World", "X", "Y", "Z"]`, which fixes each gizmo's emission order name-first.
- `setup_chip_tests`' no-G54-on-Setup2's-op clause narrows to plane chips (`" · "`): the `G54` origin name is Setup1's own, legitimately - the law was about op chips, and it still holds there.

## Tested

- Red first: with only the pins committed, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- gizmo_tests axis_note_tests` ran 8 failed / 7 passed, exactly the new and re-pinned label tests - e.g. the fresh world's labels were `["X", "Y", "Z"]` with no name.

- Full lib: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` - 382 passed, 0 failed (5 ignored). An earlier run of the same command failed only on `structural::shell_structure_light`, a theme-sync test this change never touches; it passes in isolation and on re-run - pre-existing parallel global-theme-state flakiness, already noted on #638.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run` builds clean (untouched crate).
- Not exercised: the on-screen labels themselves - the producers are pinned instead.

Requested by @spikeypineapple on #616. Smoothing differs per control, and the "auto" behaviour is maximum accuracy on finishing, with roughing aggressiveness following the stock left. The design was posted on the issue before code.

- **The option:** **"Smoothing per operation"**, a new document post option (`PostOptions.smoothing`), **off by default**.
  - **Off:** no smoothing PARAM is in the stream, so every program, and the `postOptions` object, is **byte-identical**.
  - **Saving:** the additive `smoothing` project key, absent when off. Undoable through `SetPostOptions`, and offered as a checkbox under the post picker for every mill post.
- **On, each operation states its ask** (`app::smoothing::of`) as `PARAM Smoothing <mm>` + `PARAM SmoothingMode finish|rough`:
  - **finish:** an op with a contour tolerance and no stock left asks **half** its tolerance (the control's deviation stacks on the verified path);
  - **rough:** an op leaving stock asks **stock × 0.2, capped at 0.25 mm, never more than that fifth** (no floor);
  - **nothing:** drilling, tapping, probing, threading, facing and the lathe kinds ask nothing.
- **Each mill post writes its control's words** after the section preamble and **undoes them at the section end**, so no tolerance leaks:

  | Post | On | Off |
  |---|---|---|
  | Tormach / LinuxCNC | `G64 P<tol>` | the header's `G64 P0.001` / `P0.025` |
  | Fanuc | one note "SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - G5.1 STATES NO TOLERANCE" (G5.1 has no tolerance word; review of #635) | none |
  | Haas | `G187 P3\|P1 E<tol>` | `G187` |
  | Siemens 840D | `CYCLE832(<tol>,_FINISH\|_ROUGH,1)` | `CYCLE832()` |
  | Heidenhain (ISO) | `G62 T<tol>` | `G62` |
  | Mazak | one note "SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - NO MAZAK FORM STATED" (no guessed word) | none |

- **Fanuc writes nothing yet:** `G5.1 Q1` states no tolerance, so it can't be held to the op's ask. A bounded form can follow with #614's Doosan sample. Decision record: `docs/decisions/616-smoothing.md`.

## How tested

- **New `crates/app/tests/smoothing.rs`, 4/4:**
  - `off_is_byte_identical_and_writes_no_smoothing_word`: every mill post.
  - `each_dialect_writes_its_words_and_undoes_them_at_the_section_end`: finish and rough per dialect; the words are stated before the first cut and reset after.
  - `mazak_names_the_ask_once_and_writes_no_guessed_word`
  - `finish_ops_ask_their_tolerance_and_rough_ops_ask_from_their_stock`: including the clamp ends and drill → none.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** post and app suites pass after the follow-up commit. The first run caught `lathe_post_g76` pinning the whole `postOptions` object; the key is now omitted when off. The only ui reds are the 3 known GPU-adapter tests (#615 / #623).

title: feat(post): the document's program number and comment, per dialect (#258 part 2)
body:
Part 2 of #258's split: the program number and comment. Today every post hard-codes `O0001` followed by the machine name. Branched from upstream/main; the fork is synced at v0.15.0.

## What changed
- **Document field:** a new `ProgramInfo { number, comment }` singleton (schema.rs). Unset means every post writes exactly what it wrote before.
- **Command:** an undoable `SetProgramInfo`. At creation it refuses by name:
  - a number outside 1-9999;
  - a comment over 40 characters, non-printable or non-ASCII, or containing `( ) % ; *`.

  Chosen: refuse rather than sanitise. Heidenhain and SINUMERIK, which use the comment as the program name, check it against their name rules at post time.
- **UI:** "Program number" and "Program comment" fields on the Post page. They commit on Enter or when focus leaves.
- **MCP:** a new `set_program` tool.
- **Scripts:** they get a `program` global `{number, numbered, comment}` (`engine::run_program_with`); `programNumber` is kept. Documented in docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md.
- **Per-operation files:** one file per op counts up from the stated number and is refused past O9999. The old code silently clamped instead.
- **Project file v59:** an optional `program` key. This is a version step, not just an added key, because an older build would drop the key and post O0001, which could overwrite a different program on the control. v58 files load with nothing set.

**Per dialect.** Each rule is cited in its .cps. The manual section references were written from memory, so a maintainer may want to check them against the manuals.
- **Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak:** `O####` (O0001-O9999), then `(<comment or machine name>)`.
- **Haas:** five-digit `O#####`, written only when a number is set.
- **Tormach PathPilot:** never an O-word, because LinuxCNC's O words are subroutine and flow-control words. A number goes in the header comment.
- **Heidenhain ISO:** the comment becomes the program name, `%<name> G71 *`, limited to file-name characters. If only a number is set, it is used as the name.
- **SINUMERIK:** the comment becomes `%_N_<NAME>_MPF` (letters, digits and `_`; the first two are letters or `_` plus a letter; at most 24 characters). A name that breaks these rules is refused, not renamed. The number goes in a `; PROGRAM n` comment.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/258-program-number.md`.

## How tested
- **New `program_info` tests (9):**
  - output is byte-identical in all 7 posts when nothing is set;
  - each dialect's header with a number and comment, and with a number alone;
  - post-time refusals;
  - command validation, undo and redo;
  - the typed-number parser (accepts `O0012`);
  - per-op numbering;
  - a live post writes `O0077 (Lid)`, and undo restores O0001;
  - round-trip: a v58 file loads with nothing set, and a corrupt value is refused.
- **Also new:** `mcp_setup::set_program_states_undoes_and_refuses_by_name`, and ui `program_info_tests` (typing into the fields, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y, a refusal).
- **Gate:** 35 app test binaries (338 tests) pass, including conformance, golden_cl, posting, every post suite, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, mcp and mcp_setup. All camcraft-post tests pass. ui lib passes 378; the one failure is the headless-GPU test, which also fails on this machine without the change. Clippy (post/app/ui, `-D warnings`) is clean. **No golden changed.**

## Not exercised
A GUI hands-on check, and a run of a numbered program on a control or in the Hub. G-code changes only when a number or comment is set.

Changelog: The document states its program number and comment (Post page, MCP set_program); each post writes it in its own dialect - O-word (Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak, Haas), Heidenhain program name, SINUMERIK %_N_..._MPF, PathPilot header comment; project v59 (#258)

title: feat(motion,app): Trochoidal slot - engagement-controlled trochoid operation (#220 slice 1)
body:
Slice 1 of #220: an engagement-controlled trochoid generator and a standalone **Trochoidal slot** operation. Branched from upstream/main; the fork is synced at v0.15.0.

## What changed
**The generator** (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/trochoid_slot.rs`, `trochoid_loops.rs`, `trochoid_air.rs`), specced from Otkur & Lazoglu 2007 and Rauch, Duc & Hascoet 2009.
- **Loop shape:** each loop is the front arc of a circle of radius ρ = B / cos 10°, with B = (W − D)/2 by default. The arc runs wall to wall and meets each wall at 10°.
  - On a straight chain the loops are shifted copies, so they never cross. Classic full-circle trochoids always cross the previous loop, and the verifier holds the post on a same-depth crossing.
  - A wall move between arcs cleans the cusp, and a fillet (the smoothing radius) blends it into each arc.
- **Start and end:** a helical bore of radius B at the start. A stepped fan of arcs closes the far end.
- **Returns:** microlift (default 0.3 mm, retracing the arc just cut at the return feed) or retract.
- **Engagement:** measured with the Adaptive pins' dexel yardstick (`quality::measure`) on each candidate level. The planner tries steps from 100% of the user's step down to 7%, and a note says when the step was cut. Adaptive's planner raster was not reused because it counts finished walls as contact (see the decision file).
- **Lifted returns over air:** a new `machining2d::lifted_cut` checks each lifted return against the in-process stock.
- **Refused by name:**
  - a channel narrower than the tool (it suggests a plain Slot);
  - a loop wider than the room;
  - a limit no step can hold (the message gives the lowest reading, where it was, and at which step);
  - a loop leaving the channel;
  - a crossing (the verifier's own `crossed_pairs`);
  - a lifted return over stock.

**The operation:** `OpType::TrochoidalSlot` (kind 39) in the ribbon's 2D mill family.
- **Authoring:** two endpoints and a width, like Slot, verified against the slot's stadium.
- **Parameters:** loop width (auto), forward step, max engagement, return, microlift height, smoothing radius, stock to leave, heights, stepdown, cutting/return/plunge feeds, climb.
- **Undo and editing:** create and edit are undoable (`CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams`). It has a small Geometry/Heights/Passes/Feeds page.
- **Project file:** a `trochoidal_slot` params entry. There is no `PROJECT_VERSION` bump, following the probe op's precedent (#108/#344) for an appended kind. Older builds won't read a document that uses the new kind.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/220-trochoidal-slot.md`.

## How tested
- **motion `trochoid_slot`** (7 tests, plus 2 unit tests):
  - A full-width slot (D10 in W16, 1 mm step) measures θmax **66.5°**; a straight Slot in the same channel measures **180°**.
  - A 60° limit forces the step down, and the note says so.
  - The verifier is clean (no crossing, gouge or rapid-in-stock) for climb and conventional, microlift and retract.
  - Microlift returns land on air, and the check catches one placed over stock.
  - Named refusals; the loops post as arcs.
- **app `trochoid_op`:** create and edit undo/redo; generate verifies clean and posts G03; a too-narrow channel is refused by name; project round trip.
- **New goldens:** `golden/trochoid_slot_small.cl` and `golden/nc/trochoid_slot_small.nc` (Fanuc, G02/G03).
- **Edited tests:** `ribbon` and `probe_op` pinned the probe as the last kind; they now pin index 38, and kind 39 is pinned.
- **Passing:**
  - motion `adaptive_band`;
  - app mill2d_b/c, ribbon, tool_law, probe_op, golden_cl, fanuc_post, project_roundtrip, operations, commands_undo, conformance, heidenhain_block_form, slot_caps, drill_prior_kinds, pick_doors, setup_align, wall_column_gouge, drilling_axial;
  - ui kind/ribbon/tab tests (including `every_registry_kind_gets_its_tab_bar`) and ui `operations`;
  - clippy on motion, app and ui (`-D warnings`).
- **Runtime:** the `trochoid_slot` binary takes about 80 s in debug when run in parallel. Each test is under 25 s alone.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **No run yet:** a GUI hands-on check, and a Hub or machine run of the posted arcs. This adds new posted G-code.
- **Deferred to later slices:** Adaptive's trochoidal mode (Done means 2), the corner-overload pin, centre-line picking from a model chain (typed endpoints today), the in-plane cutting return, feed reduction where engagement rises, and wall finishing when the loop band is narrower than the room.

Changelog: Trochoidal slot operation: an engagement-controlled trochoid along a typed centre line - measured contact angle held under a limit by adapting the step, microlift or retract returns, named refusals (#220, slice 1)

body:
**Stacked on #551** (EDM machine kinds). Its commits show here until #551 merges; this PR adds one commit on top.

## What changed

`edm.conditions[]` in the `.mch` `edm` section (#531, part of #290, design D4):
- Each condition is `{ id, name, gap, wire_diameter | undersize, role: rough|skim|finish, notes }`. It holds only the geometry a toolpath needs. Power and flushing stay the control's, selected by `id`.
- `id` is the control's own selector, required and unique; a numeric id reads as its word. Lengths scale with the file's unit. Gap and undersize may be 0; a wire diameter must be positive.
- A garbled entry refuses the file, naming its id, and `is_sane` restates the law for project files.
- `Edm::condition(machine, id, need)` is the door the first EDM op (#532) calls at command creation. A missing condition, or an unstated field the op needs (gap, wire diameter, undersize), is refused by name before any generator runs.
- No conditions ship. Tests use an explicitly synthetic table.

title: feat(ui): preview the incoming stock in the viewport on the setup page
body:
**Replaces #429** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

## What changed
While a setup's settings page is open and its stock source is "What <previous setup> leaves behind", the viewport draws the incoming body as a translucent **teal** closed block, in the active setup's frame, distinct from the setup's own Stock node.

- App: new `setup_stock_view::incoming_shape(world, setup)` calls `stock_sim::incoming_body` once and returns the box/volume plus `body.display().surface(&[])` as triangles mapped into the viewport's frame (`A_active * inverse(A_setup)`; identity when the setup is active). An empty body or sheet is an error naming the setup; a bad index is skipped, never a panic.
- UI: `incoming_view::IncomingView` caches it keyed by (setup, active setup, `doc_version`) - measured once per document version, never per frame - refreshed at the end of `drain_actions` and cleared the moment the page closes, another page opens, or the setup switches to its own stock. A failed measurement is logged once and draws nothing.
- Drawing: `collect_parts` adds a stock-type part with vertex class 4; `fs_stock` paints class 4 as teal rgb (0.12, 0.66, 0.74) at alpha 0.45 in the existing translucent stock pass.
- **Closed block** (after the GUI check of 2026-11-09 showed nothing teal): `setup_stock_shell::floor_and_walls` closes the incoming body (floor, walls and top), so the preview shows even where the top sheet would sit inside the part.
- **Drawn after the traced stock:** the preview is an overlay part (`viewport::is_overlay`) that `viewport::draw_order` sorts after the stock parts the traced whole-program view replaces, so it stays visible over it.
- The page's incoming box/volume text reuses the viewport's measurement, so there is one program sim per version instead of two.
- Display only: no command, nothing undoable (ephemeral view state per AGENTS.md). No files #412 touches were edited (`stock_sim*.rs`, `operation/*`, `rest/*`).

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1718 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). title: build: Docker builds for the shipped Linux target (and documented cross/native rules)
body:
## What changed

A `docker/` directory (local tooling - no workflow, no Actions minutes) with a per-target answer for every release.yml asset:

| Shipped target | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 tar.gz / deb / rpm / AppImage | `docker/linux.Dockerfile`: `ubuntu:22.04` pinned by digest (runner distro, glibc 2.35), release.yml's apt list verbatim (+ `build-essential ca-certificates curl file`, preinstalled on the runner, absent in a bare image), the same `cargo build --locked --release -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post`, `scripts/package-linux.sh` + `scripts/package-appimage.sh` with the same pinned linuxdeploy URL and SHA-256, and the job's package-content checks. Rust pinned by `RUST_TOOLCHAIN` build arg (default 1.99.1). `--output type=local,dest=dist` writes the four packages to the host. AppImage needs no FUSE (the script only `--appimage-extract`s linuxdeploy). |
| Snap, Flatpak | Stay on the runner jobs: snapcraft needs snapd, flatpak-builder needs bwrap namespaces - both mean a `--privileged` container. Documented. |
| Windows zip + Inno installer (msvc) | Stays native: msvc target, ISCC.exe and signtool are Windows-only; cargo-xwin would bake Microsoft's CRT/SDK into an image. Documented. |
